checks.description: Actual intake binds receipt to parsed bytes and refuses changed/unreadable lock; deterministic baseline comparison and final-boundary tests.
Relevant intake/path/download and assembly regressions pass without production gate relaxation or network/hardware claims.

constraints.text: Bind parsing and SHA-256 to the same captured bytes; after archive verification refuse changed, deleted or unreadable lock content without emitting a successful completion receipt, and return the captured digest without a later pathname rehash. Deterministic actual-intake tests must show baseline false success versus candidate refusal, unchanged success, same-byte replacement, and replacement after comparison reporting captured A. State the boundary explicitly: no perpetual pathname stability, A-to-B-to-A detection or authenticated provenance claim.

Keep tests entirely offline with tiny mocked responses and isolated scratch fixtures; retain receipt shape, inspection with zero output/network activity, unprivileged execution, fresh-output and path/symlink/raw-target/overlap refusals, retry exhaustion and archive size/hash failures. Refused intake may retain partial output for diagnosis, but it is not a completed intake and cannot be silently reused. Preserve the baseline and before/after evidence; no full recovery rebuild or VM/physical boot is needed for this receipt claim.

Preserve independent assembly archive/control checks and completion continuity plus integration-input freshness enforcement. A changed builder must never be accepted with stale assembly by altering historical receipts or waiving a gate. Retain historical accepted image evidence at its original revisions, keep physical G4/H04/H07/H12 dependencies open, and obtain a fresh independent delivery verifier over the actual complete candidate diff and evidence before claiming offline receipt closure. Limit production changes to the proposed intake repair, tests and dated evidence; factory geometry, rollback, persistence, heater/idle policy, profiles, upstream pins and recovery admission remain accepted requirements.

decision.rationale: Reviewed actual source at dfc3c5461e8ae57e5dd373fe8504c28269fb4775, locally accessed 2026-10-01. scripts/recovery_image.py:258-282 parses lock.read_text(), verifies archives against those entries, then returns sha(lock); replacement A-to-B can therefore yield a successful receipt naming B although A selected the archives. This is source-derived evidence, not executed reproduction; the supplied planner plan is likewise source-derived. tests/test_recovery_image.py has no executed-intake continuity regression and its inspection test exercises assemble. docs/hardware/host-os-tasks.md:135 and docs/remaining-work-plan.md:157-174 explicitly require this repair. ADR 0014 requires separate unprivileged pinned intake, offline assembly, fresh ignored paths and supported-builder retirement; the accepted independent-image proposal preserves factory 8 GB geometry, recovery capacity, provenance and refusal gates; ADR 0010 preserves independent recovery, data and idle admission. A single parsed-and-hashed byte snapshot plus final content comparison provides a concrete before/after improvement: misleading baseline success becomes explicit refusal for changed/unreadable completion input, while unchanged content yields the captured digest. Standard-library hashing fits the existing custom integration gap; advisory locking adds coordination without excluding uncooperative writers. No duplicate accepted workflow, new dependency, spending, licensing change, hardware claim or owner scope expansion is introduced. Resource impact is one lock-sized captured buffer and one completion read/hash on the workstation, with tiny isolated mocked fixtures; no image geometry or guest runtime budget change. Source review is sufficient for design approval, but runtime regression and fresh independent delivery verification remain required. Approval grants no hardware, network, boot-policy or release authority.
